source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 19. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

title.en: Caring for family in hard times

learn.en: Even before he became a prophet, the people of Makkah called Muhammad ﷺ al-Amīn — the Trustworthy.
learn.title: Al-Amīn

learn.en: Allah later said about him: “And indeed, you are of a great character.” (Qur'an 68:4)
learn.title: A great character

learn.en: Khadījah described him: he keeps family ties, helps the weak, gives to the poor, honours guests and helps people in hard times. (Bukhari 3)
learn.title: What he did

learn.en: Once, a famine hit Makkah. His uncle Abu Ṭālib had a big family and little money. The Prophet ﷺ and his uncle al-ʿAbbās each took one of Abu Ṭālib's sons to look after: al-ʿAbbās took Jaʿfar, and the Prophet ﷺ took ʿAlī.
learn.title: The famine

learn.en: Abu Ṭālib had looked after Muhammad ﷺ when he was an orphan. Now he paid back that kindness. (Qur'an 93:6)
learn.title: Paying back kindness

quiz.en: What did the people of Makkah call Muhammad ﷺ?
Whom did the Prophet ﷺ take into his home?
True or false? Abu Ṭālib looked after the Prophet ﷺ when he was an orphan.
True or false? Real help means sharing the load.

think.q: Who has helped you in your life? How could you help them back?
think.a: Maybe a grandparent, teacher or friend — a visit, a du'aa or a helping hand repays kindness.

parents.summary: Before prophethood, Muhammad ﷺ was al-Amīn. In a famine he took ʿAlī into his home to help his uncle Abu Ṭālib, who had raised him.
parents.tip: Do one practical act of help for a relative this week together.
